outcome.technical: WHAT WAS ALREADY STAGED: neither suite. At HEAD both ended in `_harness.run(_cases)`; the description's sentence calling test_guard_edits.py staged is wrong, as the coordinator said. STAGED NOW: both, `__main__` = `_harness.staged_main` over a literal STAGES table; `_selftest()` removed, as in the staged neighbours (test__output.py, test__deps.py). test_journal_writes.py blocks (cases; slot-seconds in sweep run 2, run 1 in brackets): jw-core `_cases` 144; 1.3 [1.6] | jw-machine-path 5; 0.2 [0.5] | jw-call-mark 5; 0.2 [0.5] | jw-one-question 10; 1.5 [1.8] | jw-link-question 4; 2.2 [2.3] | jw-generated 4; 60.6 [59.6] | jw-topology 1; 2.0 [2.0] | jw-slot 1; 0.9 [0.9] | jw-created-file 13; 3.7 [3.8] | sn0 `_switch_reading_cases` 25; 22.2 [22.1]. The sn0 block's label is `sn0`: before staging a raise there was reported as `sn0 the switch-reading cases`, and a raising block is reported under its STAGES label. test_guard_edits.py blocks: ge-core 47; 0.3 [0.3] | ge-config 66; 0.5 [0.4] | ge-volume-pair 5; 1.5 [1.7] | ge-link 7; 8.7 [8.7] | ge-generated 4; 71.4 [68.9] | ge-process-count 2; 1.6 [1.6] | ge-registration 4; 5.9 [5.9] | ge-member 5; 1.9 [2.1] | ge-relative-registration 4; 1.0 [1.0] | ge-topology 3; 2.1 [2.2]. Moved into shared fixture functions so a block can run alone: `_suite_cfg()` (the cfg `_cases` built inline), `_worktree_fixture(check)` (the worktree pair plus its failing tf0 case, so a block whose own build fails is red, not short of cases), and the wrappers `_config_block_cases` / `_volume_pair_block_cases`, which build their own project dir, cfg and pair. The journal's main body stays one block: its sections took 1.0 s of 83.9 s in process (profile), and each block costs a process start. A HIDDEN DEPENDENCY BETWEEN BLOCKS was found by running each block alone: cf37b (ge-process-count) went red alone, because a cold process's first decide lists 4 of the plugin's scripts/ folders (`_config.find_script` walking to `_journal_io.py` for `_config.journal_lib()`), and in the one-process run an earlier block had already loaded that library. The block now calls `_config.journal_lib()` before it counts, with a comment saying why; cf37b's assertion is unchanged. FINDING for the batch, not fixed: cf37b has only ever measured a warm process, and the real hook is a cold process on every call, so each hook run pays that scripts/ walk. Two stale sentences in test_journal_writes.py (docstring line 18, comment by j4) said `_harness.run` reports a vanished function; now `_harness.stage` does, and they say so. LABEL DIFF: before = HEAD's files run whole; after = the staged whole run. Case ids and verdicts, in order: identical, journal 212/212, guard 147/147 (`diff` exit 0; files labels.before.txt/labels.after.txt/labels.diff under the scratch dir sg2.8/journal and sg2.8/guard). The full label text differs only in run-varying details: hashes, timestamps and seconds (12 journal lines, 4 guard lines). With those masked the guard diff is empty, and the journal differs on sn9 alone, where the detail's repr lists the same two rows in the other order. Its assertion sorts them (`sorted(str(r[0]) ...)`), so this is the read order of the trail, not a change. EACH BLOCK ALONE, reverse table order, fresh scratch cwd/TMPDIR each (each_block_alone.py, exit 0): every block exit 0 with all cases passing; the blocks sum to 212 and 147 = the whole runs. FLOOR GUARD: code moved out of `_cases` into STAGES rows and shared fixtures, and that is the move the guard reports. No assertion changed; the evidence is the label diff and each block's green run alone. The one added statement (`_config.journal_lib()`) restores the state cf37b was always measured in, and the mutation table shows removing it turns cf37b red alone. COST TABLE: departs from the coordinator's 'targeted local --record-costs' on evidence. The table is a windows table (platform windows-2025, recorded from windows cells per the runner's comment), and tests/test_stamp_verification.py swp4 pins that: platform_family(doc.platform) must be win32. A local --record-costs writes platform=darwin; the intermediate table after my local runs had `darwin`, which swp4 refuses. It would also give darwin figures to heavy windows blocks: test_drive_phase ar18-block, windows 235.1 s, would drop to the 300 s floor while taking about that long on windows. So: (1) `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_journal_writes.py tests/test_guard_edits.py --jobs 4 --record-costs .github/sweep-costs.json`, twice with a 4-minute gap: the two suites' blocks, measured locally, the only place they can be measured until CI runs them. (2) `python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py --costs-from-log <windows cells of runs 44573316400 (all eight), and the two saved cells each of the third and fourth runs, concatenated> --platform windows-2025 --workers 4 --record-costs .github/sweep-costs.json`, which printed `recorded 199 files' seconds and 285 blocks'`. That run keeps the platform windows-2025 and merges the local block figures, so each staged suite's file figure is its blocks' sum (jw 94.8, ge 94.9). Caveat: those 20 block figures are this machine's (darwin) under a windows label, until the next windows run's logs are recorded. All 49 swept files the line added or grew (git diff --name-only de21866c HEAD) are timed, none estimated. Stale ones: test_build_shop.py 85.8 comes from a windows run that FAILED (exited 1) before it grew to 78 cases, and test__floor_guard.py has staged_main but CI runs it whole, so it has a file figure and no block figures. TIMEOUT ARITHMETIC (runner's rule, block_timeout = max(300, ceil(TIMEOUT_PER_COST 3 x figure))): ge-generated 71.4 -> ceil(214.2) = 215 -> 300 s; jw-generated 60.6 -> 182 -> 300 s. On a runner 6x slower, ge-generated would take 71.4 x 6 = 428 s > 300, and jw-generated 364 s > 300: both would be killed. The ratio these runs show is smaller. Local sweeps of HEAD's files took 92.6/92.5 s then 91.2/91.3 s (two runs, 4-minute gap); windows took 236.1 s (guard) and 240.8 s (journal) in run 44573316400, about 2.6x, and the fourth run killed both at 300 s, so at least 3.2x. At 3.3x, ge-generated is about 236 s and jw-generated about 200 s: under the 300 s block timeout, but at about 0.79 and 0.67 of it. The CI deadline is 1800 s within a 33-minute job, and the table's longest calibrated timeout is 706 s (drive_phase ar18-block, printed by tt5). RULE 6 IS NOT MET, AND I DID NOT SPLIT: each generated block is heavier than its suite's other nine blocks together (ge 71.4 vs 23.5; jw 60.6 vs 34.2). All of that weight is one case each: cf36 (with cf36b-d, which read cf36's sweep results `seen`/`worlds`) and oq5 (oq5b-d are separable, but only 2.9 s). cProfile of `_generated_cases`: 73.3 s; 27.7 s building 364 worlds with 1497 git calls, about 20 s in the hook's own git calls inside decide (_config, 2496 calls), the rest in process. A split that keeps the labels does not exist: rule 2 and acceptance (1) forbid it, rule 6 asks for it. Options for the coordinator: (a) cut cf36/oq5 into per-family cases (new ids, so the label diff changes); (b) a cheaper world fixture, e.g. a copied template repo instead of init/add/commit per world, which removes up to 1092 of the 1497 fixture git calls; (c) accept a 300 s block at about 0.7-0.8 of it on windows. WALL: the two suites in one sweep took 91.5 s wall before and 73.8 s after (--jobs 4).
